pr.title: fix(Send Email Node): Allow non-inline file attachments
pr.body: ## Summary The Send Email node always set a `Content-ID` (`cid`) on every attachment, marking them as `Content-Disposition: inline`. Email clients that honor MIME semantics (Outlook, OWA) then hide non-referenced files from the attachments list, so users were sending files that recipients never saw. This PR keeps the existing field's behavior intact and adds an explicit second field for regular attachments: - **Attachments (Inline)** — existing `attachments` option, unchanged behavior (still sets `cid: ` for embedding via ``). Renamed displayName and updated description to make the inline semantics obvious. - **Attachments (File)** — new `fileAttachments` option. Binary properties listed here are attached without a `cid`, so they appear in the recipient's attachments list as regular files. Both fields accept the same comma-separated binary-property syntax. Entries from both are concatenated into `mailOptions.attachments`. ### Backward compatibility The internal name `attachments` is preserved, so existing workflow JSON keeps working with no migration. Users who *want* their files to stop being inline move them to the new field. ### Why not auto-detect? An earlier approach (PR #25716) auto-detected `cid:` references in the HTML body. Explicit user control is more predictable, avoids parsing user-authored HTML, and aligns with the first solution proposed by the issue author. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts Fixes #24333 ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code. - [ ] PR title and summary are descriptive. ([conventions](../blob/master/.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md)) - [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created. - [ ] Tests included. - [ ] PR Labeled with `Backport to Beta`, `Backport to Stable`, or `Backport to v1` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported)
